conviction_note: Measurement 3a sums to +5.0, mostly one company-level fact: a $164.4m backlog (+22.5% YoY, 'faster turns') plus an Aug-26 in-quarter deck saying wafer-fab sales 'remain strong', set against a revenue bar (~$58.5m, -12% q/q from $66.2m) that I could source only once. Measurement 3b: abs_move 14% (implied 13.05%, own median 12.75%, thin coverage, short interest at a 12-month high) and p_up 60, which gives +2.8. The scaled number sits below the sum because the revenue bar is single-sourced, the backlog is public, and the CFO, COO and directors sold about $2.6m during the quarter being reported. Both pull p_up toward 50.
bar: EPS $0.09 for FQ1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-08-29), from the MarketBeat consensus (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RELL/earnings) and Northland's $0.09 (cut from $0.11, 2026-07-29, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-northland-securities-estimate-for-rell-q1-earnings-2026-07-29/). Two agreeing sources, though Northland is likely inside the consensus. Revenue bar about $58.5m, ONE source only (a search snippet attributed to a MarketBeat/Zacks-type forecast). Sizes that depend on revenue are capped. The company gives no formal guidance. Comparables: FQ4 FY26 $66.2m / $0.21 non-GAAP; FQ1 FY26 $54.6m / $0.13.
positioning_check: Short interest 925,687 shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement: 9.22% of float (MarketBeat) or 6.3% of shares (Equibles), 8.99 days to cover, up 6.6% from 868,020 and roughly 3.2x the 289,910 of 2025-10-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/rell/shortinterest ; https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RELL/short-interest). With about 9 days to cover on 123k shares/day, the short is crowded for this float. Options: 25d skew -1.71 vol pts (calls slightly richer), put/call OI 0.28, ATM IV 100.9%, event-implied move 13.05%. The market leans 'balanced' to slightly bullish. Run-up +6.6% over 5 days and +8.5% over 20; stock 13.4% below its 52-week high (about $21.8, reached after the July print) and 100% above its 52-week low.

findings.finding: Year-end backlog was $164.4m, +22.5% YoY and +8.7% q/q, the highest in three years. The company's Aug-26 deck says current backlog 'includes faster turns than prior years'. Against that, the revenue bar for the reported quarter (FQ1 FY27, Jun-Aug) is about $58.5m, which is 12% below the $66.2m FQ4 just printed and only +7% on FQ1 FY26's $54.6m. The EPS bar is $0.09 against $0.21 non-GAAP in FQ4. Q1 has not historically been a seasonal step-down: FQ4 FY25 $51.9m to FQ1 FY26 $54.6m. Holding even about $62-64m of revenue at 31% gross margin clears both bars.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue/EPS beats have been bought hard: FQ4 FY26 revenue +19.6% vs estimate gave +21.15%; FQ3 FY26 (+4% revenue beat, EPS $0.07 vs $0.05) gave +22.7%; FQ1 FY26 ($54.6m vs $51.5m) gave +11.78%. An in-line EPS (FQ2 FY26, -$0.01 vs -$0.01) gave -11.73% despite a revenue beat, and a revenue miss (FQ3 FY25) gave -17.06% (MarketBeat earnings table + baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage is 2-3 analysts (Northland, Sidoti). Both cut FQ1 estimates after the July beat (Northland $0.11 to $0.09, Sidoti lower) while Northland raised FY27 to $0.62, so the street has pushed growth out of FQ1. If the backlog were priced into the quarter, the revenue estimate would sit near the $66m run rate rather than $58.5m, and the stock would not have given back the whole post-print move (from about $21.8 to $17.5 in August; $18.90 now, below the $21.14 post-print close).
findings.independence: The FQ4 release reports the same backlog numbers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000355948/000119312526312436/rell-ex99_1.htm). On the Q4 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-22-richardson-electronics-ltd-stock/) management cited combined PMT/GES backlog +24.8% and Canvys book-to-bill 1.3, and said a GE-platform wind order for a Canadian site 'did ship in Q1'. All are company sources. The revenue bar is single-sourced, and the deck also says 'timing of new orders can vary quarter-to-quarter'.

findings.finding: The deck management presented on 2026-08-26, three days before the reported quarter closed, says 'Semiconductor wafer fab sales remain strong' and 'Key customers forecasting growth for the remainder of CY2026 and into CY2027'. The 10-K shows one PMT customer (by context the semi wafer-fab customer) at $31.5m, 14% of FY26 sales, against none above 10% in FY25. The largest growth line therefore has an in-quarter company statement behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Semi wafer fab drove the FQ1 FY26 beat (+52% YoY semi wafer fab sales; stock +11.78%) and the FQ4 FY26 PMT +28.1% (stock +21.15%).
findings.why_not_priced: The deck sits on the company site and was presented at a small-cap conference. No wire carried the 'remain strong' line, and both estimate cuts came before it. Had it been priced, the FQ1 estimate would not be below FQ4 by 12%.
findings.independence: Shares a document with finding 1 (one deck, two different lines: backlog vs in-quarter semi demand). Customer concentration comes from the 10-K, filed 2026-08-03 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/355948/000035594826000002/rell-20260530.htm). Risk: one 14% customer makes the line lumpy.

findings.finding: Semiconductor equipment peers who spoke after RELL's July call all point up through RELL's Jun-Aug quarter. Advanced Energy (RF power, the closest analog) posted Q2 2026 semi revenue $278m, +27% q/q, and guided Q3 total revenue to $640m vs $574m. Lam guided its Sep quarter to $8.1bn vs $6.72bn in June. Applied Materials guided FQ4 Semiconductor Systems revenue to about $7.9bn, +62% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separately observable; WFE strength reached RELL through the PMT beats above.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public macro facts and they are priced in the WFE names. The question is transmission to a $260m distributor-manufacturer whose estimates were cut after these prints were known, which suggests analysts have not carried the WFE ramp into RELL's FQ1.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a RELL number. Independent sources: Lam (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3533702/lam-research-corporation-reports-financial-results-for-the-quarter-ended-june-28-2026) and Applied (https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-third-quarter-2026-results). Partly overlaps finding 2 in direction, but the source is different.

findings.finding: Insiders sold about $2.57m of stock in the 90 days to early October with zero purchases (MarketBeat). The sales came mid-quarter, inside the reported quarter: CFO Robert Ben 9,000 shares at $21.61 (2026-08-04), COO Wendy Diddell 23,901 at about $20 (2026-08-04), director Kluge 29,000 at $17.90 (2026-07-30), and directors Belin, Benham and Halverson in early to mid August. EDGAR shows a Form 4/144 cluster from 07-22 to 08-24.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observable; insider sales after the July print coincided with the stock falling from about $21.8 to $17.5 in August.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Form 4s are public and the stock fell in August. Not priced as a signal about FQ1, because the officers who sold, including the CFO, knew the quarter-to-date run rate at the time.
findings.independence: EDGAR Form 4 list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000355948&type=4&dateb=&owner=include&count=40); COO sale (https://kalkinemedia.com/us/news/announcements/richardson-electronics-coo-wendy-diddell-sells-23901-shares-at-20-each). Caveat: these are open-window sales right after a +21% print, some following option exercises, which is routine and shrinks the finding. A crowded short (9 days to cover) also argues against sizing a negative large.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 925,687 shares (2026-09-15 settlement), 9.22% of float, about 9 days to cover, roughly 3.2x the October 2025 level. Shorts have built into a print on a name whose last two beats moved +21% and +23%, on 123k shares/day of turnover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Post-beat moves of +21.15% and +22.7% on the last two prints with short interest already rising; misses have also moved -11.7% to -17%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning amplifies a beat rather than signing the print. Calls are slightly richer than puts (skew -1.71, put/call OI 0.28), so the options market is not leaning against the shorts either. Filed small and two-sided.
findings.independence: MarketBeat short-interest page gives the same figures (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RELL/short-interest).

findings.finding: The 'multimillion-dollar BESS order' management promised on the July call for Q1 was announced on 2026-08-20: 18 systems, 7 MWh, for seven remote Alaska communities, with completion by end-2027. It counts as a FQ1 booking, but revenue lands mostly later.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BESS has not yet been a reported line that moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the order is public. What it adds is that the call can confirm the promised Q1 booking was delivered, supporting backlog/book-to-bill, which is the line the call is judged on.
findings.independence: The Q4 call quote 'we expect to announce a multimillion-dollar order for our BES systems in Q1' (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-22-richardson-electronics-ltd-stock/).

findings.finding: GE Vernova's Q2 2026 Wind segment: orders $1.2bn, -40% organically on lower North American onshore equipment, partly offset by higher onshore services. RELL's GES (about 10-13% of sales, $6.5m in FQ4) sells retrofit pitch-energy modules for GE and other platforms, which are services/aftermarket exposure. On 2026-08-26 RELL said wind module demand was 'steady/increasing'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GES lumpiness has contributed to past misses (FY25 prints), but it is a small segment.
findings.why_not_priced: Public. Equipment weakness and services strength offset each other for an aftermarket supplier, so it is sized at zero; filed so the panel can weigh it.
findings.independence: RELL deck slide 18 (same deck as findings 1-2) says wind module demand is steady or increasing.

findings.finding: Margin risk, inferred: FQ4 gross margin was 31.2% vs 31.6% a year earlier. The 10-K says gross margin 'could be negatively impacted' if tariffs cannot be passed through. FQ1 mix shifts toward BESS integration (Gotion cells, Alaska program), which is likely lower-margin than engineered tubes and wind modules. The EPS bar of $0.09 is low enough that this matters mainly on a revenue shortfall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS in line with a revenue beat (FQ2 FY26) gave -11.73%, so the stock trades on EPS quality as well as revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference, not a disclosed number. Filed small.
findings.independence: 10-K tariff language (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/355948/000035594826000002/rell-20260530.htm). No direct counterparty confirmation.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the mildly call-bid skew (-1.71) and the low put/call OI. Against it: the +8.5% 20-day run-up means part of a beat is already bought, and shorts at 9 days to cover show informed money leaning the other way. Net, p_up is held at 60 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar verification): the revenue bar of $58.5m is single-sourced, so finding 1 is cut from +4.0 to +3.0, p_up from 62 to 60 and print_vs_bar from +7 to +6. Lesson 8 (thin coverage, company-level number) argued for keeping it large, which is why it was not cut further.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): the WFE peer finding goes from +1.0 to +0.8 and the margin inference from -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 7 (crowded short against a negative): the insider-selling finding goes from -1.0 to -0.7, with short interest recorded in positioning_check.
Lessons 1, 2, 3, 4 and 9 left everything standing. Reaction history supports beats being bought, no one-offs or financing were filed, and findings are net of segments (wind sized 0 against semis).
